title: Systems and automation for consultants and coaches
meta_description: Creosote Labs consolidates the booking, CRM, invoicing, and spreadsheet tools of a consulting or coaching practice into one system and automates the rest.
h1: Systems and automation for consultants and coaches
intro: A consulting or coaching practice often accumulates one tool per task: a booking link, a CRM such as HubSpot or Dubsado, a course platform such as Kajabi or Thinkific, QuickBooks for invoices, and a Google Sheet that tracks which clients are active, what package they bought, and how many sessions remain. Those tools rarely share data, so the owner often re-enters the same client information several times and reconciles the sheet by hand.

Creosote Labs builds a single system of record for the practice, with clients, engagements, sessions, and payments in one place. We connect the booking tool, invoicing, and email to it so a completed session updates the client's remaining balance and a finished package triggers the renewal conversation. Repetitive steps such as sending pre-session forms and generating engagement letters are automated. The system is documented and handed over to the practice.
projects: A client tracker that replaces the spreadsheet, showing each engagement's package, sessions used, and next scheduled date.
An onboarding automation that sends the engagement letter, intake questionnaire, and payment link when a client signs.
A session-count system that deducts from a package when a Calendly or Acuity booking is marked complete and flags packages near their end.
A monthly invoicing process that creates QuickBooks invoices for retainer clients without manual entry.
A group program roster that tracks cohort members, attendance, and homework submissions in one view.

faqs.q: Which existing tools stay and which get replaced?
faqs.a: That is decided in the operations review, which costs $3,000 and takes one day. Tools that work well, such as a booking link or QuickBooks, usually stay and get connected; the spreadsheets that track clients, packages, and sessions are what get consolidated.

faqs.q: What happens to the client history in the current spreadsheet?
faqs.a: Existing client, package, and session records are migrated into the new system as part of implementation. The practice supplies the current spreadsheets and exports from any tool being replaced.
